claims.text: Emicizumab (bispecific Ab that replaces factor VIII funct) for hemophilia A, subcut every 1, 2 or 4 wks.
claims.quote: For hemophilia A, emicizumab, a recombinant humanized bispecific monoclonal antibody that binds to both factor IX and factor X and links them into a factor Xase–like active complex that obviates the need for factor VIII, is an effective treatment (2). Emicizumab is administered as a subcutaneous injection every 1, 2, or 4 weeks
Fitusiran is a small inhibitory RNA that knocks down the production of the natural anticoagulant protein, antithrombin
Concizumab is a humanized monoclonal antibody that blocks tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI)
Marstacimab is a humanized monoclonal antibody against TFPI
Other therapeutic agents used for both hemophilia A and B include fitusiran, concizumab, and marstacimab
Concizumab can also be used for treatment of hemophilia A or B with inhibitors

claims.text: Antifibrinolytics (aminocaproic acid, tranexamic acid) may also be used as adjuncts after dental extraction or oral mucosal trauma.
claims.quote: An antifibrinolytic agent (aminocaproic acid or tranexamic acid) may also be used as adjunctive therapy in hemophilia A or B to suppress fibrinolysis and prevent late bleeding after dental extraction or other oropharyngeal mucosal trauma

claims.text: Emicizumab label: routine prophylaxis in hemophilia A ± factor VIII inhibitors, newborn and older.
claims.quote: routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in adult and pediatric patients ages newborn and older with hemophilia A (congenital factor VIII deficiency) with or without factor VIII inhibitors
